channel.title: Methodology Feed
channel.description: Aggregated research articles from Nature Biotechnology and Nature Methods.

item.title: Nature Biotechnology: Quantifying endosomal escape in vivo to guide lipid nanoparticle design
item.description: Nature Biotechnology, Published online: 11 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41587-026-03047-x A lysosomal barcoding strategy to quantify endosomal escape of nucleic acids in vivo assesses the performance of branched ionizable lipids for potent liver delivery.

item.title: Nature Biotechnology: In vivo endosomal escape assay identifies mechanisms for efficient hepatic LNP delivery
item.description: Nature Biotechnology, Published online: 11 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41587-026-03022-6 Endosomal escape of lipid nanoparticles is quantified and optimized in vivo.

item.title: Nature Biotechnology: Engineered TnpB genome editors for plants and human cells identified by ribonucleoprotein mutational scanning
item.description: Nature Biotechnology, Published online: 11 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41587-026-03059-7 TnpB endonucleases are engineered for improved genome editing.

item.title: Nature Methods: AF2BIND: predicting small-molecule binding sites using the pair representation of AlphaFold2
item.description: Nature Methods, Published online: 11 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41592-026-03011-2 AF2BIND is a logistic regression model trained on AlphaFold2 pair features to predict small-molecule binding-site residues in proteins, without multiple sequence alignments, homology models or knowledge of the true ligand. AF2BIND was used to predict binding sites across the AF2-predicted human proteome, finding thousands of potentially new ligandable sites.

item.title: Nature Biotechnology: The promises and challenges of neoantigen cancer vaccines
item.description: Nature Biotechnology, Published online: 10 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41587-026-03018-2 Surveying recent progress in neoantigen cancer vaccine development, this Review highlights areas where further technological advances and optimized trial design could enhance clinical impact.

item.title: Nature Biotechnology: B cell depletion in autoimmune disease: in vivo CAR-T or T cell engagers?
item.description: Nature Biotechnology, Published online: 10 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41587-026-03069-5 Deep B cell depletion is delivering transformative clinical results in autoimmune diseases. Dealmakers are wagering on the best tools for the job.

item.title: Nature Methods: Oligomeric symmetrical scaffolds for resolving RNA structures by cryoEM
item.description: Nature Methods, Published online: 09 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41592-026-03017-w We have engineered symmetric RNA scaffolds that allow structure solution of small RNAs via single-particle cryogenic-sample electron microscopy (cryoEM). This method enabled small-molecule ligand placement in experimental maps and revealed the molecular basis for specificity of natural and synthetic RNA aptamers, thus suggesting routes for structure-guided RNA engineering.

item.title: Nature Methods: Toward a unified framework for determining conformational ensembles of disordered proteins
item.description: Nature Methods, Published online: 09 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41592-026-03003-2 This Perspective establishes a comprehensive and practical framework to guide intrinsically disordered protein (IDP) ensemble determination, benchmarking and interpretation, as well as proposes a roadmap for IDP ensemble determination, uncertainty quantification and actionable benchmarking strategies.

item.title: Nature Methods: Scaffolds with optimized quaternary symmetry for de novo cryoEM structure determination of small RNAs
item.description: Nature Methods, Published online: 09 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41592-026-03016-x Engineered RNA domains that can adopt two- and fourfold symmetry are shown to be effective scaffolds for structure determination for RNAs otherwise too small for cryoEM.

item.title: Nature Biotechnology: Re-evaluating the site-directed nuclease classification as a regulatory trigger for genome-edited plant products
item.description: Nature Biotechnology, Published online: 05 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41587-026-03028-0 Site-directed nuclease (SDN) classification into SDN-1, SDN-2 and SDN-3 outcomes is used for regulating genome-edited plant products in some countries. This reductive categorization system fails to cover the breadth of genome editing technologies developed over the past decade and their rapidly approaching commercial use. Here, we argue that, in the context of plant breeding, regulations should focus on the characteristics of the genome editing outcome, rather than specific methods used in the development process. Such a science-based, outcome-focused regulatory approach would future-proof the risk-proportionate oversight of plant breeding innovations and enable a more efficient delivery of improved crop varieties amidst growing concerns of climate change and evolving pests and diseases.

item.title: Nature Methods: Large-scale library of 3D ant images captured with synchrotron X-ray microtomography
item.description: Nature Methods, Published online: 05 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41592-026-03004-1 This study introduces an unprecedented resource of thousands of 3D images representing the diversity of an ecologically dominant group of insects: ants. These data were generated using high-throughput synchrotron X-ray microtomography, which opens a pathway to scalable digitization of the vast diversity of invertebrate life.

item.title: Nature Methods: High-throughput phenomics of global ant biodiversity
item.description: Nature Methods, Published online: 05 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41592-026-03005-0 Antscan is a publicly accessible database of synchrotron X-ray CT images of ants. The database covers almost 800 species from more than 200 genera and is coordinated with genome sequencing projects that will enable integrative analyses.

item.title: Nature Biotechnology: Quantification and transcriptome profiling reveal abundant, dynamic and translatable dephospho-CoA-capped RNAs
item.description: Nature Biotechnology, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41587-026-03040-4 An enzyme that specifically recognizes dephospho-CoA (dpCoA)-capped RNAs is used to quantify dpCoA-RNAs in cells.

item.title: Nature Methods: It’s a colorful pangenome world
item.description: Nature Methods, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41592-026-03021-0 A pangenome can reveal the spectrum of genome variation within a species. The toolbox for working with pangenomes is filling up.

item.title: Nature Biotechnology: Sharing big data for sustainable agri-food innovation
item.description: Nature Biotechnology, Published online: 03 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41587-026-03052-0 Sharing big data for sustainable agri-food innovation

item.title: Nature Methods: A unified framework for multiomics deconvolution
item.description: Nature Methods, Published online: 02 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41592-026-03008-x The new algorithm DECODE transcends the limitations of omics-specific methods, and provides a unified framework for the deconvolution of transcriptomic, proteomic and metabolomic datasets.
